# CyberBuddy

> Browser security assessment suite: clickjacking validation, security header grading (A–F / 0–100), CSP policy auditing, CORS posture checks, a DNS & domain security analyzer, a local-only CSRF PoC generator, and the local-only JWT Security Workbench (decode/verify, VAPT test payloads, edit & re-sign) — with evidence-grade output.

- Hub: https://amitpal-cyberbuddy.github.io/CyberBuddy/
- Tools catalog: https://amitpal-cyberbuddy.github.io/CyberBuddy/tools/
- Guides: https://amitpal-cyberbuddy.github.io/CyberBuddy/guides/
- Documentation: https://amitpal-cyberbuddy.github.io/CyberBuddy/documentation/
- Methodology: https://amitpal-cyberbuddy.github.io/CyberBuddy/methodology/
- Source: https://github.com/AmitPal-CyberBuddy/CyberBuddy

## Tools

- Clickjacking Validator (`/tools/clickjacking/`) — X-Frame-Options + CSP frame-ancestors + live iframe proof. OWASP WSTG-CLNT-09, CWE-1021.
- Security Headers (`/tools/headers/`) — CSP, HSTS, XFO, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP/COEP/CORP, cookie flags. OWASP WSTG-CONF-07/12, CWE-693.
- CORS Validator (`/tools/cors/`) — ACAO reflection vs allowlist, credentials, Vary: Origin. OWASP WSTG-CLNT-07, CWE-942.
- CSP Policy Auditor (`/tools/csp/`) — enforced vs Report-Only CSP, effective script/style sources, navigation controls, mixed content, syntax, Trusted Types, and reporting. OWASP WSTG-CONF-12, CWE-79, CWE-693.
- DNS & Domain Security Analyzer (`/tools/dns/`) — public-DNS posture: SPF, DMARC, DKIM, DNSSEC, CAA and name-server redundancy, graded 0–100 with the raw record behind each finding. RFC 7489, RFC 7208, RFC 6376, RFC 4033, CWE-290.
- CSRF PoC Generator (`/tools/csrf/`) — paste a raw Burp request, get a standalone HTML proof-of-concept (forms and fetch variants, READY/LIMITED/NOT DIRECTLY REPRESENTABLE). Fully local: nothing sent, stored, or relayed. OWASP WSTG-SESS-05, CWE-352.
- JWT Security Workbench (`/tools/jwt/`) — decode, inspect, verify, edit and re-sign compact JWS tokens locally: strict parsing, claim timeline and observations, HMAC/RSA-PKCS#1/RSA-PSS/ECDSA verify and sign with a key you supply, a semantic original-vs-modified diff, local RSA test-key generation and explicit TEST TOKEN labels (copy/download never exports key material by accident). JWT-03 adds labelled test-variant templates (alg:none, claim tamper/re-sign, algorithm confusion with a pasted public key, embedded JWK, jku/x5u, kid) and bounded HS256/384/512 secret testing in a Web Worker with progress, cancel and explicit limits. Decoding also yields prioritized, severity-tagged VAPT testing suggestions with one-click TEST PAYLOADs (copyable raw or as a Burp `Authorization: Bearer` header) and 2–3 Burp Suite verification steps each. The token's `alg` is never trusted to choose the verifier (algorithm-confusion guard). Fully local. RFC 7519, RFC 7515, OWASP WSTG-SESS-10, CWE-347.

## Guides

Short, tool-connected notes — one per tool. Each guide covers one weakness, how to confirm it with the matching tool, and closes with primary references (OWASP, CWE, MDN, specs) for depth. Guides are intentionally concise; they are not a full article library.

- Clickjacking (`/guides/clickjacking/`) — UI redressing, why X-Frame-Options alone is insufficient, how CSP frame-ancestors decides framing, and how to produce screenshot evidence with the Clickjacking Validator. OWASP WSTG-CLNT-09, CWE-1021.
- Security Headers (`/guides/headers/`) — which response headers earn their place, why X-XSS-Protection should be 0, HSTS and Referrer-Policy semantics, and how to read the letter grade the Security Headers tool prints. OWASP WSTG-CONF-07, CWE-693.
- CORS (`/guides/cors/`) — reflected Origin plus credentials as a read of authenticated responses, allowlist mistakes (prefix/suffix/regex, `null`, wildcard with credentials), Vary: Origin, and how to confirm it with the CORS Validator. OWASP WSTG-CLNT-07, CWE-942.
- CSP (`/guides/csp/`) — reading a policy for what it actually blocks: fallback chains, 'unsafe-inline' versus nonces, Report-Only versus enforced, directives a <meta> tag drops, and how the CSP Policy Auditor grades them. OWASP WSTG-CONF-12, CWE-79.
- CSRF (`/guides/csrf/`) — the three conditions that make an action forgeable, why the PoC is the finding, what READY / LIMITED / NOT DIRECTLY REPRESENTABLE mean, and the fix. OWASP WSTG-SESS-05, CWE-352.
- JWT (`/guides/jwt/`) — header/payload/signature, decoding versus verification, time and issuer/audience claims, symmetric versus asymmetric algorithms, `alg:none`, algorithm confusion, `kid`/`jku`/`x5u`/embedded JWK, replay/lifetime, and how the Workbench verifies, signs, templates, derives prioritized VAPT test payloads, and bounded-tests locally with the key you supply. RFC 7519, RFC 7515, OWASP WSTG-SESS-10, CWE-347.
- DNS (`/guides/dns/`) — SPF, DMARC, DKIM, DNSSEC and CAA: what each record actually protects, what a missing one really risks, and how the DNS & Domain Security Analyzer grades the whole posture from public DNS. RFC 7489, RFC 7208, RFC 6376, RFC 4033, CWE-290.

## Documentation

`/documentation/` is the operator page: local quick start (`python3 server.py`, loopback bind, `--allow-private`), which of the three engines answers a scan, the five Python CLI entry points and their exit codes, evidence/export formats and provenance, the limits of the static GitHub Pages build (no response headers, so no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options/HSTS), and what leaves the browser. Scoring rules live at `/methodology/`, not there.

## How scans run

1. Python engines (`server.py` or optional Vercel `api/`) when reachable.
2. Same-origin published reports at `cache/<host>.json` for the demo targets listed in `urls.txt` (GitHub Actions, every 6 hours).
3. In-browser graders, a direct CORS read, then opt-in third-party header relays. HTTP checks are non-destructive: a GET baseline plus analyst-selected HEAD/OPTIONS and CORS preflight simulation; CyberBuddy never sends POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE to a target.
4. The DNS & Domain Security Analyzer reads public DNS through the system resolver locally, or a consent-gated DNS-over-HTTPS lookup (Google Public DNS) on the hosted site. It never connects to the target's own servers.

## Constraints

Authorized testing only. Do not scan systems without permission. Results are advisory, never a guarantee of safety. Cloud-metadata and link-local targets are always blocked.

## Privacy

Scan history is stored only in the user's browser (localStorage, 24h expiry); it is never uploaded and never shared between users. Published reports cover only the fixed demo targets in urls.txt, never user-submitted URLs. Third-party header relays (hackertarget.com, allorigins.win, corsproxy.io, codetabs.com) are opt-in, receive the hostname only by default, and their results are labelled unverified. The DNS analyzer's hosted fallback sends the domain name and its parent labels needed for inherited CAA checks to dns.google after consent; records returned that way are labelled unverified.
